slides.title: Satan never told Adam: "Disobey Allah."
slides.promise: The Evil I finds where the fall began: a moment before the hand reached the tree.

slides.head: The fall began in the heart
slides.body: Humanity didn't begin to fall when Adam stretched out his hand. It began a moment before, when the question inside his heart changed.

slides.head: He redirected Adam's gaze
slides.body: Satan knew a heart at peace with its Lord doesn't openly embrace rebellion. So he never began by inviting Adam to disobey.

slides.quote: O Adam, shall I lead you to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that never fades away?
slides.source: The whisper as the Qur'an records it, Surah Ta-Ha, verse 120

slides.head: Notice what is missing
slides.body: There's no call to disobey, only the offer of something better. All of it turns on the self: what it will gain, possess and become.

slides.head: Temptation turns you towards yourself
slides.body: It rarely begins by pulling us away from Allah. It begins by drawing our attention towards ourselves.

slides.head: Wanting was not the sin
slides.body: Desire is part of the nature Allah created within us. The danger came when desire grew louder than obedience.

slides.head: His struggle was with himself
slides.body: The tree didn't come searching for him. Its fruit didn't call his name.

slides.head: How temptation begins
items: The fall began in the heart, before the hand.
The whisper held no call to disobey.
It offered something better, all of it for the self.

slides.head: Read more in The Evil I
